territorial_scope.description: Applies to advertisements placed before the public in New York State, as stated in subdivision 2 of the amended section, which subdivision 3 applies to.

evidence.quote: placed before the public, in this state

summary.short: Requires persons who create or produce commercial advertisements for property or services to conspicuously disclose a synthetic performer's presence where they have actual knowledge. Civil penalty: one thousand dollars for a first violation, five thousand dollars for subsequent violations. Takes effect 180 days after becoming law.
summary.long: Amends General Business Law section 396-b, which governs advertisements, by adding definitions and new subdivisions. Subdivision 1 defines artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and synthetic performer; a synthetic performer is a digitally created asset intended to create the impression of a human performer who is not recognizable as any identifiable natural performer. Subdivision 3 applies to persons engaged in dealing in any property or service who, for any commercial purpose, produce or create an advertisement in any medium, and requires them to conspicuously disclose that a synthetic performer is in the advertisement where they have actual knowledge. A violation carries a civil penalty of one thousand dollars for a first violation and five thousand dollars for any subsequent violation. Subdivision 4 excludes advertisements and promotional materials for expressive works, provided use of a synthetic performer is consistent with its use in the work. Subdivision 7 excludes audio advertisements and uses of artificial intelligence solely for language translation of a human performer. Subdivisions 5 and 6 preserve rights under Civil Rights Law sections 50, 50-f and 51 and other law, and the protections of 47 U.S.C. section 230. Subdivision 8 states that the section does not apply to advertising media by whom an advertisement is published or disseminated. Section 2 is a severability clause. The act takes effect on the 180th day after it becomes law.

relations.note: Section 1 amends § 396-b to read as set out in the bill. The amended section adds definitions, a disclosure duty for advertisements using a synthetic performer, exemptions, and a civil penalty.

notes: The bill is shown as plain text with no underlining or brackets, so new wording cannot be separated from restated unchanged wording of § 396-b in this document. Section 1 also cites the section's history ('as added by chapter 1031 of the laws of 1965'); this is not coded as a relation. Section 3 sets the effective date at the 180th day after the act becomes law. No registry instrument is referenced in the text, so target_instrument_id is empty for all rows. thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment. The dollar amounts in Sec. 1 subd. 3 (civil penalty for first and subsequent violations) are enforcement amounts, not thresholds. The 180-day effective date in Sec. 3 is a procedural time limit, recorded as an event, not a threshold.
